rows.reason: page states the amendment updates the page limit for the Community Benefits Plan; it does not say every battery-materials solicitation requires a plan, so the claim was narrowed to this FOA (opened 2023-11-15, closed 2024-03-19)

corrections.claim: Cirba Solutions (Sept 2024) was selected to enter award negotiation with DOE for up to $200 million, so the funding was not final at selection

rows.reason: page (2024-09-20) states selection to enter into award negotiation for up to $200 million under the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law; the label 'Round 2' is not on the page
page (2025-10-21) states DOE's Office of Manufacturing and Energy Supply Chains canceled more than $700 million in grants, citing 'missed milestones' and projects that 'were not economically viable'

doe_award.program: Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, DOE Office of Manufacturing and Energy Supply Chains (selected for award negotiation; program round not named on page)

rows.reason: page (2024-09-20, Charlotte NC dateline) states selection for up to $200 million for a lithium-ion processing facility in Columbia, South Carolina making battery-grade salts; one search for cancelled/terminated found no Cirba-specific cancellation, but the award was only a negotiation selection and the search did not reach a DOE termination list entry

cited page (2025-03-04) says the $316 million pCAM grant remains active, but electrive (2025-10-21, https://www.electrive.com/es/2025/10/21/us-cancels-funding-for-ascend-elements-and-other-battery-companies/) reports DOE cancelled the $316 million Ascend Elements grant for the Hopkinsville KY plant in October 2025 (about $206 million already disbursed, about $110 million remaining) and a 2026-04-13 teaser headline reports Ascend insolvency; the cited page does not support a status correction
